Found 4 of them (2 NRRD-FRAME-001, 1 NRRD-SPACE-001 partial, 1 NRRD-SPACE-001 preservation_only) all cite the same missing capability: the NRRD0005 'measurement frame' field had no typed parser, no cardinality validation, no measurement-to-world transform, and no read-time version gate -- only a version-requirement trigger existed (NrrdDocument.version_requirements() bumping to NRRD0005 when the field is present). inputs.acceptance_evidence: Built measurement_frame.py as a deliberately SEPARATE module from space.py (a sibling obligation's own explicit 'keep NRRD0005 measurement-frame transforms in a separate model and API' instruction, confirmed directly in the SAL register, not assumed): MeasurementFrameTransform (space_dimension, columns, .measurement_to_world()) and build_measurement_frame_transform(), reusing space.py's own parse_space_directions() for the identical (v0,v1,...) vector syntax rather than duplicating a parser, but enforcing EXACTLY space_dimension vectors (the obligation's own literal wording) and rejecting 'none' entries (measurement frame has no per-axis concept, unlike space directions). The transform is a pure linear map with no origin term, confirmed directly against the spec text ('the matrix transforms... coordinates in the measurement frame to coordinates in world space', no translation mentioned), distinct from SpaceTransform.index_to_world's own affine map. Added the read-time NRRD0005 version gate to reader.py's own _load(), mirroring the exact precedent already established for LIST/printf multi-file declarations under a pre-NRRD0004 magic (NRRD-MULTIFILE-001, this same session) -- confirmed the field was genuinely unenforced at read time before this fix (only the separate, opt-in validate() call caught it).
